text:
mara: Quick sync — we need a concise error taxonomy for the automatic fallback policy UX. Current problem: operators can’t tell whether a fallback was triggered for infra flakiness vs model-quality regression.

jon: +1. We should separate triggers into two orthogonal dimensions: source (infra | model | client) and severity (soft | hard).

lee: Agree. Example: infra GPU OOM or node eviction -> soft degrade (retry/requeue to cheaper variant). Model hallucination / low-quality -> hard degrade (route to human or safe-model).

sam: UX ask: show both the trigger type and the evidence behind it. e.g., show the metric names and a mini-plot: `infra.errors.gpu_oom` spike, `model.quality.delta` drop.

mara: That means the rollout console needs fields: trigger_label, trigger_metric, trigger_window, confidence_score, and last_sampled_prompt id. Also a link to the audit trace.

jon: Prototype config snippet (for the policy editor):
```yaml
autofallback:
  triggers:
    - id: infra-high-5xx
      source: infra
      condition: "sum(rate(infra.http_5xx[1m])) > 0.05"
      severity: soft
      actions: [route: cheaper-model, notify: ops]
    - id: model-low-confidence
      source: model
      condition: "avg(model.response_confidence[5m]) < 0.4"
      severity: hard
      actions: [route: safe-model, open-ticket: true]
```

lee: Nice. Need to standardize metric names and window semantics in the editor help text. Operators keep asking what `confidence` actually means.

anna: UX note: show an example request/response snippet in the audit panel that caused the trigger. Redact PII by default with an inline toggle.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary policy v2 applied to customer-prod-2 at 2025-03-11T10:12:05Z :rocket:

sam: We also need an explainability panel: show which predicates matched and the sampling of matching traces. E.g., `matched_predicates: ["http_502_spike","kv_cache_miss"]`.

mara: Question: If both infra and model predicates fire at the same time, prefer the higher severity. But we should record both in the audit log.

jon: Implementation detail: audit log entry schema should include fields: `root_cause_tags` (list), `trigger_scores` (map), `matched_metrics` (list). For the UI we can flatten to human text: "Model-confidence dropped 0.35 -> triggered hard fallback; concurrent infra 5xx spike recorded."

lee: For telemetry queries, suggest a canonical promql example in the devdocs: `sum(rate(infra.errors{job=~"model.*"}[5m])) by (error_type)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(model.latency_bucket[5m]))` so console can show p95 and spike charts.

tess: Edge case: transient client malformation -> should be client source, severity soft, but not count against model quality SLAs. We need a flag `affects_quality_sla: true/false` in the audit entry.

mara: UX wireframe idea: timeline for a rollout decision showing events: metric sparks -> predicate matched -> fallback executed -> rollout metric delta. We can animate the matching predicates when you hover.

sam: We should surface a small reproducible artifact in each audit entry: a deterministic seed + sanitized prompt + snapshot of model outputs so SREs can replay locally. Put a TTL on artifacts (30d).

anna: Permissions: only rollout-owners and SRE can view full request/response. Others see summarized/redacted view. Add `view_level` to audit entries.

jon: Back to UX labels — propose standardized language: "soft degrade (auto-retry/alt-model)", "hard degrade (manual review/safe-path)", "quarantine (pause rollout)". Add short tooltip text for each.

lee: One more: oscillation protection. If a policy flips between fallback and primary more than 3 times in 10m, mark it as 'flapping' and escalate to manual. Show a red badge in the rollout list.

mara: Great. Action items:
- jon: draft audit log schema doc + sample entries (due EOD)
- lee: add promql examples to devdocs + label definitions (tomorrow)
- sam: wireframe panel with mini-plot + trace snippets (prototype next week)
- anna: RBAC matrix for audit visibility (end of week)

tess: Quick question — do we want the console to allow manual reassign of root cause if SRE fixes labeling? e.g., mark an event as "misclassified".

mara: Yes. Add a lightweight "reclassify" action on audit entries that records who changed it and why. Keep original classification immutable.

ops-bot: [incident-bot] New incident created: ROLLOUT-452 — flapping detected on canary policy v2 (linked).

jon: Looks good. I'll start on the schema. If anyone has sample traces we can use for the prototype, drop them in #eng-platform-uploads with `autofallback-sample` tag.

lee: Will do. Also add a small glossary in the policy editor modal: define `confidence`, `quality_sla`, `severity`, `source`.

mara: Thanks all. If no major objections, we'll merge the UX brief and start a small spike on telemetry + audit retention. :thumbsup:

sam: +1

anna: +1

lee: +1

jon: +1
